title: Belgium occupies Ruanda-Urundi after defeating Germany
note: Belgian forces occupied Ruanda April-May 1916 and Urundi June 1916; League of Nations mandate granted 1922 (event states 1923 — minor date error). Core claim fully confirmed.

title: Belgian administration introduces ethnic identity cards
note: Belgian colonial government introduced ethnicity-classified ID cards after 1933, codifying Hutu/Tutsi/Twa. Widely documented across multiple authoritative sources.

title: Hutu Manifesto published, demanding political equality
note: Bahutu Manifesto published 24 March 1957 by nine Hutu intellectuals including Kayibanda. Actually called for Tutsi political disfranchisement, not merely equality — description softens its content, but year and authorship confirmed.

title: Rwandan Social Revolution — Hutu uprising against Tutsi rule
note: November 1959 uprising, 'Wind of Destruction' (muyaga) terminology, and mass Tutsi exodus to Uganda, Burundi, Congo all confirmed.

title: Rwandan monarchy abolished; republic proclaimed
note: Coup of Gitarama January 28, 1961; monarchy abolished, republic proclaimed. Kayibanda named PM (not president at this stage — he became president at independence). Substantively accurate.

title: Rwanda achieves independence from Belgium
note: Rwanda independent July 1, 1962; Kayibanda first president. Date and core facts exactly confirmed.

title: Tutsi exile raids trigger massacres inside Rwanda
note: Inyenzi raids from Burundi in December 1963; government reprisals killed an estimated 10,000-20,000 Tutsi civilians. Core event confirmed.

title: Kayibanda wins single-party elections; Parmehutu consolidates power
note: Kayibanda's one-party rule and ethnic quotas are documented, but no specific confirming source found for 1965 uncontested elections as a discrete event.

title: General Habyarimana seizes power in coup
note: Coup July 5, 1973 confirmed; MRND created 1974 (not immediately as text implies). Core facts verified.

title: MRND single-party state formalized; Habyarimana consolidates control
note: MRND created 1974-1975 as sole legal party with automatic membership for all Rwandans; ethnic quotas confirmed. Verified.

title: New constitution and Habyarimana re-election by referendum
note: A 1978 constitution is historically plausible but no direct confirming source found for the 98% referendum claim in searches conducted.

title: RPF founded among Tutsi exiles in Uganda
note: RPF was formally founded December 1987, not 1985. RANU (precursor) formed 1979. The year 1985 is incorrect per multiple sources.

title: RPF invasion begins the Rwandan Civil War
note: RPF invaded October 1, 1990 from Uganda with ~2,500 fighters. Rwigyema killed on second day; Kagame returned from US to take command. All core facts confirmed.

title: France and Belgium intervene militarily to back Habyarimana
note: France deployed 600 troops (Operation Noroît) to directly block RPF advance. Belgium took a more neutral diplomatic role and did not militarily back Habyarimana — description overstates Belgian military intervention. French role fully confirmed.

title: Rwandan constitution amended to allow multi-party politics
note: Multi-party constitution amendment June 1991 under donor pressure is well documented. Core facts confirmed.

title: Interahamwe militia organized by Hutu extremists
note: Interahamwe formed ~1990-1992 as MRND youth wing; trained and armed by Presidential Guard; pre-prepared kill lists used in genocide. All core claims confirmed.

title: Arusha Accords signed between Habyarimana and RPF
note: Signed August 4, 1993 in Arusha, Tanzania, brokered by Tanzania and OAU. Provisions on transitional government, RPF integration, refugee return all confirmed.

title: UNAMIR peacekeeping mission deployed to Rwanda
note: UNAMIR deployed under General Dallaire per UNSC Resolution 872 (October 1993). January 11, 1994 Genocide Fax warning ignored by UN HQ confirmed.

title: Habyarimana's plane shot down — genocide begins
note: April 6, 1994 plane shot down killing Habyarimana and Burundian president Ntaryamira. Presidential Guard and Interahamwe began systematic killings within hours using pre-prepared lists. All confirmed.

title: Assassination of Prime Minister Uwilingiyimana and UN peacekeepers
note: Uwilingiyimana murdered April 7, 1994; ten Belgian UNAMIR peacekeepers killed; Belgium subsequently withdrew its UNAMIR battalion. All core facts confirmed.

title: Radio Mille Collines broadcasts incitement to mass murder
note: RTLM broadcasted inyenzi (cockroach) dehumanization and directed killers to locations. Three RTLM leaders convicted at ICTR for genocide/incitement. All confirmed.

title: UN Security Council reduces UNAMIR force amid genocide
note: UNSC Resolution 912 on April 21, 1994 reduced UNAMIR from 2,500 to 270 personnel. Confirmed.

title: Nyamata and Ntarama church massacres
note: Nyamata: ~10,000 killed April 14-19, 50,000 buried at memorial. Ntarama: 5,000 killed April 15. Event states '40,000 victims' combined — actual burial count at Nyamata alone is 50,000. Undercount in description but not false.

title: Bisesero massacre — Tutsi resistance overwhelmed
note: Bisesero Tutsi resistance using stones and spears confirmed; ~50,000 killed there; French soldiers reached survivors in late June but delayed intervention is documented and controversial. Confirmed.

title: Operation Turquoise — French military intervention in western Rwanda
note: France launched Operation Turquoise June 22, 1994 per UNSC Resolution 929; Zone Turquoise in southwestern Rwanda. Critics document that it allowed genocidaires to escape into Zaire. All confirmed.

title: RPF captures Kigali and ends the genocide
note: RPF captured Kigali July 4, declared ceasefire July 18, 1994. Estimated 500,000-800,000 killed in ~100 days. All confirmed.

title: Mass Hutu refugee crisis — two million flee to Zaire
note: ~2 million Hutu refugees fled to Zaire/Tanzania; Goma camps became genocidaire militia bases. All confirmed.

title: Transitional Government of National Unity formed
note: Bizimungu as president, Twagiramungu as PM, Kagame as VP and defense minister with RPF holding effective control. Confirmed.

title: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established
note: ICTR established November 8, 1994 by UNSC Resolution 955; based in Arusha, Tanzania. First international court to convict specifically for genocide. Operated until December 2015. All confirmed.

title: Kibeho massacre — RPF soldiers kill Hutu displaced persons
note: April 22, 1995; Australian UN observers estimated at least 4,000 killed by RPA. Rwandan government claimed 338. No senior prosecutions conducted. All core facts confirmed.

title: Gacaca community justice system conceptualized
note: Gacaca formally legislated 2001 and national by 2005 — confirmed. The specific 1995 conceptualization date is plausible but no confirming source found.

title: First Congo War — Rwanda invades Zaire to destroy genocidaire camps
note: Rwanda and Uganda sponsored Kabila's AFDL from late 1996; Kabila seized power May 1997, renamed country DRC. Primary motive was destroying ex-FAR/Interahamwe camps. All confirmed.

title: Rwanda pursues genocidaires into Congo; civilian massacres documented
note: UN Mapping Report documented systematic massacres of Hutu civilians by Rwandan and allied forces; 'several tens of thousands' killed. Rwanda attempted to block publication. All confirmed.

title: Second Congo War — Rwanda turns against Kabila and re-invades DRC
note: Kabila expelled Rwandan troops July 27, 1998; Rwanda/Uganda invaded August 2, 1998. War killed estimated 5.4 million. Rwanda supported RCD rebel movement. All confirmed.

title: Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement signed
note: Lusaka Ceasefire signed July 10, 1999 by DRC, Zimbabwe, Angola, Namibia, Uganda, Rwanda. Fighting continued for years in eastern Congo. All confirmed.

title: Paul Kagame becomes president
note: Bizimungu resigned March 2000; Kagame elected by transitional assembly and sworn in April 22, 2000. Confirmed.

title: Vision 2020 development blueprint launched
note: Vision 2020 launched by Kagame government targeting middle-income status; ICT, tourism, services emphasis confirmed.

title: Gacaca courts legislated to process genocide cases
note: Gacaca formally legislated 2001; processed ~1.9 million cases; praised for scale, criticized for limited due process and exclusion of RPF crimes. All confirmed.

title: Pretoria Peace Agreement — Rwanda withdraws from DRC
note: Pretoria Accord signed July 2002; Rwanda withdrew troops in exchange for DRC dismantling FDLR. Withdrawal completed October 2002 but FDLR remained active. Confirmed.

title: New constitution adopted by referendum
note: Constitutional referendum May 26, 2003; approved by 93% of voters; bicameral parliament with 30% women quota; banned ethnicity-based parties. All confirmed.

title: First multiparty presidential elections — Kagame wins with 95%
note: August 25, 2003 elections; Kagame won 95.05%; climate of fear and harassment documented. All confirmed.

title: Rwanda bans political parties based on ethnicity or region
note: Constitutional ban on ethnic/regional parties implemented; Forum of Political Parties established; critics noted selective application to suppress genuine opposition. Confirmed.

title: Gacaca courts go fully national; mass releases of genocide suspects
note: Gacaca expanded nationally to ~9,000 cell jurisdictions in 2005; large-scale confession-based releases. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda and France sever diplomatic relations over genocide accountability
note: November 2006 Rwanda severed relations after French judge Bruguière issued arrest warrants for nine Kagame aides. Relations restored 2009. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda abolishes the death penalty
note: Death penalty abolished July 25, 2007; motivated partly by extradition needs from abolitionist European states. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda's economy achieves sustained high growth
note: GDP growth rates of 7-11% confirmed by mid-to-late 2000s; World Bank recognition of Rwanda as top reformer confirmed.

title: Rwanda joins the Commonwealth
note: Rwanda admitted to Commonwealth at 2009 CHOGM (event year 2008 is one year early — admission was 2009). Second country with no British colonial ties (after Mozambique). Core claim confirmed with minor year correction needed.

title: UN Panel accuses Rwanda of supporting CNDP rebels in eastern DRC
note: December 2008 UN Group of Experts report documented Rwanda's support for CNDP/Nkunda including weapons, financing, command integration. Aid suspended. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda joins the East African Community
note: Rwanda formally joined EAC in 2007, not 2009. The year tag is incorrect by two years. EAC customs union deepening in 2009 is real but is not the same as joining.

title: Kagame re-elected with 93% in second presidential election
note: Kagame won 93.08% in August 2010. Campaign marked by assassination of opposition figures, journalist murder, party bans. All confirmed.

title: ICTR completes major genocide convictions
note: ICTR completed major trials by 2010 including Kambanda guilty plea and RTLM media executives. Landmark precedents on genocide and media responsibility confirmed.

title: Gacaca courts conclude operations after 1.9 million cases
note: Gacaca formally concluded in 2012 (event year tag 2011 is off by one year) after ~1.9 million cases. Core claim confirmed with minor year discrepancy.

title: M23 rebel movement emerges in eastern DRC with alleged Rwandan backing
note: M23 emerged April 2012; UN Group of Experts November 2012 report documented Rwanda's direct military support. Aid suspended by US, UK, Germany, EU. All confirmed.

title: Western donors suspend aid over M23 support allegations
note: US, UK, Germany, EU suspended/withheld aid to Rwanda following UN Expert Panel report. Confirmed.

title: M23 defeated; Rwanda-DRC relations slowly normalize
note: M23 defeated November 2013 by DRC army and UN Force Intervention Brigade. Relations did not truly normalize — description overstates reconciliation, but defeat date confirmed.

title: Constitutional referendum removes presidential term limits
note: December 2015 referendum (~98% approval) removed term limits; enabled Kagame third term 2017 and potentially keeps him in power until 2034. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda's Vision 2020 progress — middle-income aspirations near
note: GDP growth sevenfold since genocide, poverty from 60% to ~39% by 2015, improved health indicators confirmed. Development success story with governance caveats confirmed.

title: Rwanda assumes AU peacekeeping leadership role
note: Rwanda one of Africa's largest peacekeeping contributors by mid-2010s; deployed to Sudan, South Sudan, CAR, Mali with thousands of troops. Confirmed.

title: Kagame wins third presidential election with 99% of the vote
note: Kagame won 98.79% in August 2017 third presidential election; two token opponents; Diane Rwigara disqualified. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda bans plastic bags — regional environmental leadership
note: Rwanda's plastic bag ban was enacted September 2008 (Law N57/2008), not 2018. The year tag is factually incorrect by a decade. The 2018 date may reflect international recognition but the policy is from 2008.

title: Kagame assumes AU Commission chairmanship
note: Kagame elected AU Chair January 2018; championed AU reform, African Continental Free Trade Area launched March 2018 in Kigali. Confirmed.

title: France-Rwanda genocide accountability review begins
note: Macron commissioned the Duclert Commission in 2019; published 2021. Rwanda established its own Muse Commission simultaneously. Confirmed.

title: COVID-19 pandemic — Rwanda among Africa's earliest and strictest responders
note: First case March 14, 2020; lockdown March 21; drones and robots deployed for enforcement and awareness. Low caseload relative to continent confirmed.

title: Paul Rusesabagina arrested and convicted of terrorism charges
note: Arrested August 2020 via Dubai-to-Kigali flight rendition; convicted September 20, 2021; sentenced to 25 years. US designated him wrongfully detained. All confirmed.

title: France formally acknowledges 'overwhelming responsibility' for the genocide
note: Macron's May 27, 2021 Kigali speech acknowledging France's 'overwhelming responsibility' confirmed. Kagame called it 'historic'. No formal apology but described as historic acknowledgment. Confirmed.

title: Rwanda deploys troops to Mozambique to fight Islamist insurgency
note: Rwanda deployed 1,000 personnel (700 soldiers, 300 police) July 9, 2021 to Cabo Delgado. Led successful retaking of Mocímboa da Praia. Confirmed.

title: M23 resurgence and renewed DRC tensions
note: M23 resumed offensive March 2022; captured Bunagana June 2022; UN reports documented Rwandan military support. EAC mediation underway. All confirmed.

title: Rwanda-UK migration deal signed
note: UK-Rwanda Migration and Economic Development Partnership announced/signed April 13-14, 2022. Supreme Court ruled unlawful November 2023; cancelled by Starmer government July 2024. Confirmed.

title: Rusesabagina released from prison
note: Released March 24, 2023 (event year tag 2022 is incorrect — release was 2023) following US/Qatar facilitation. Year tag is off by one year but event is real.

title: EAC and SADC regional force deployed to eastern Congo amid M23 crisis
note: EACRF deployed November 2022, mandate expired December 2023; SADC SAMIDRC deployed December 2023 with South Africa, Tanzania, Malawi. EAC tensions between Rwanda and Kenya/Uganda confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Luanda peace talks on DRC-Rwanda conflict
note: Angola-brokered Luanda Process ongoing through 2023-2024; July 2024 ceasefire signed but quickly violated; Angola ended mediation March 2025. All confirmed.

title: Kagame wins fourth presidential term with 99% of the vote
note: Kagame won 99.18% in July 15, 2024 elections; sworn in August 2024 for fourth term. Only two token opponents authorised. Confirmed.

title: M23 captures Goma — DRC conflict reaches critical escalation
note: M23 with documented Rwandan military support captured Goma January 27-31, 2025. Event year 2024 reflects the escalation build-up; actual capture was January 2025. Core claim confirmed.

title: Rwanda's Vision 2050 launched; sustained development despite governance concerns
note: Vision 2050 launched targeting upper-middle-income by 2035, high-income by 2050. GDP grew 7.9% in 2024. Human rights restrictions documented alongside growth. Confirmed.
